items.reason: Everything this item names already operates (blocking repo SAST + Actions policy in sast.yml and check:ci, blocking full-history gitleaks and reporting npm audit in supply-chain.yml, a blocking lockfile-provenance test, a pre-commit secret scan, and a top-level least-privilege permissions block in all 11 workflows); the one genuinely open piece — pinning the 52 first-party actions/* refs to commit SHAs — cannot be done offline because resolving a tag to a SHA needs the GitHub API, and inventing one breaks the workflow rather than pinning it.

lessons: This repository already encodes its own D9 posture as machine-checked policy (scripts/actions-pin.mjs rules P1-P10, .github/workflow-permissions.json, .github/contract-ledger.json), and it records WHY a rule is still exempt plus the exact command that would close it — read .github/contract-ledger.json before proposing a supply-chain change, because the open item and its remedy are usually already written down there (P4/P6 explicitly say 'no offline session can do this').

Adding a fix here is a two-part diff by construction: a new workflow, job or token scope must land together with its entry in .github/workflow-permissions.json, and any exception or threshold must land with the ceiling/floor in .github/contract-ledger.json — a one-part diff turns `npm run actions:check` / `contract:ledger:check` red, so an offline agent that 'helpfully' adds a workflow breaks the build it cannot run.

Scanner 'missing' lines can contradict the scanner's own observations (here it asked for top-level `permissions:` blocks it had just measured as 11/11 present); check the tree before treating a recommendation's remedy list as the gap.
